_comment_family: Sharp Grotesk is a family of ninety-odd cuts: five weights across
many widths, numbered rather than named — 'Bold 20' is one width of
the Bold. The file's own typographic family is 'Sharp Grotesk' with
'Bold 20' as the subfamily, and asking for 'Sharp Grotesk' alone
would let any other of those cuts answer. At this family's spread of
widths that is not a subtle difference: a title measured against one
width and drawn in another overflows the block outright.
So the full name is what is declared — the same reason
gilroy-extrabold declares its subfamily and rift declares its cut.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the Windows full name (name ID 4), which is also the
PostScript name here and what the installer registers the face
under; the second is the same name spaced the way a font menu lists
it. Both name this one cut rather than the family, so a machine
answering to either is answering with this file.
